title: Emet
subtitle: Evangelical claims, the verses they cite, and the TaNaKh passages listed in answer
status_note: UNVERIFIED DRAFT (2026-11-13). Listed from general knowledge of the passages usually cited on each side. Not yet checked against Rabbi Singer or any other rabbinic source, and not attributed to anyone.

claims.claim: Isaiah 7:14 foretells that the Messiah would be born of a virgin, fulfilled in the birth of Jesus.
Micah 5:2 foretells that the Messiah would be born in Bethlehem, fulfilled in the birth of Jesus there.
Hosea 11:1, 'out of Egypt have I called my son', is a prophecy fulfilled when Jesus returned from Egypt.
Jeremiah 31:15, Rachel weeping for her children, was fulfilled in Herod's killing of the children of Bethlehem.
The prophets foretold that the Messiah would be called a Nazarene.

passages.note: No verse in the TaNaKh has the words Matthew quotes. This is one of the verses usually proposed as its source.
No verse in the TaNaKh has the words Matthew quotes. This is one of the verses usually proposed as its source.

claims.claim: Isaiah 53 describes the Messiah suffering and dying for the sins of others, fulfilled in Jesus.
Psalm 22:16, 'they pierced my hands and my feet', foretells the crucifixion.
Psalm 22 foretells Jesus's words on the cross and the dividing of his garments.

passages.kjv: the title, which the KJV does not number

claims.claim: Zechariah 12:10, 'they shall look upon me whom they have pierced', foretells the piercing of Jesus.
Jeremiah 31:31-34 foretells a new covenant, established by Jesus, that replaces the covenant made at Sinai.
Isaiah 9:6 calls the Messiah 'The mighty God', showing that he is divine.
Daniel 9:24-27 foretells when the Messiah would come and that he would be killed before the Second Temple was destroyed.
Psalm 110:1, 'The LORD said unto my Lord', shows that the Messiah is David's divine Lord.
Psalm 2:7, 'Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee', speaks of Jesus as the Son of God.
Psalm 2:12, 'Kiss the Son', commands homage to the Son of God.
Genesis 3:15, the seed of the woman, is the first prophecy of the Messiah.
The promise to Abraham's 'seed' is in the singular and so means one person, Christ.
Genesis 49:10 foretells that the Messiah (Shiloh) would come before the sceptre departed from Judah.
Deuteronomy 18:15-19 foretells Jesus as the prophet like Moses.
Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness of sin.
No one is righteous; all have sinned and cannot be righteous before God.
All people inherit sin and guilt from Adam.
One righteous person can die to atone for the sins of others.
God accepted the death of a man as a sacrifice for sin.
God became a man in Jesus.
Genesis 1:26, 'Let us make man in our image', shows a plurality of persons in God.
Deuteronomy 6:4 uses 'one' in the sense of a compound unity, which allows for the Trinity.
The Law of Moses was ended or set aside by Christ.
Anyone who does not keep every part of the Law is under a curse, and no one can keep it.
Habakkuk 2:4 teaches that the just shall live by faith, not by works of the Law.
Abraham was counted righteous by faith alone, apart from works.
Psalm 40:6-8 foretells the incarnation: 'a body hast thou prepared me'.
The thirty pieces of silver and the potter's field were foretold by the prophet Jeremiah.

passages.note: They are in Zechariah; Matthew names Jeremiah.

claims.claim: Zechariah 9:9 foretells the Messiah's entry into Jerusalem on a donkey, fulfilled by Jesus.
Psalm 41:9 foretells the betrayal of Jesus by Judas.
Psalm 69:21 foretells that Jesus would be given gall and vinegar.
Psalm 34:20 foretells that none of Jesus's bones would be broken.
Psalm 16:10 foretells the resurrection of the Messiah.
The Scriptures foretold that the Messiah would rise on the third day.
The Messiah had to come before the Second Temple was destroyed.
Isaiah 40:3, the voice crying in the wilderness, foretells John the Baptist.
John the Baptist was the Elijah foretold by Malachi.
Isaiah 9:1-2 foretells the Messiah's ministry in Galilee.
Isaiah 61:1-2 was fulfilled in the ministry of Jesus.
Psalm 118:22, the stone which the builders refused, speaks of Jesus.
The messianic prophecies Jesus did not fulfil will be fulfilled at his second coming.
Jesus is the heir to David's throne through the genealogies in Matthew and Luke.
Jeremiah 23:5-6 names the Messiah 'THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS', showing that he is God.
Proverbs 30:4, 'what is his son's name', shows that God has a Son.
Psalm 45:6-7, 'Thy throne, O God', addresses the Messiah as God.
Jesus is a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, replacing the priesthood of Aaron.
Zechariah 13:6, the wounds in his hands, speaks of the crucified Jesus.
Daniel 7:13-14, the Son of man coming with the clouds of heaven, speaks of Jesus.
Psalm 68:18 foretells the ascension of Jesus.
Isaiah 42:1-4, 'Behold my servant', speaks of Jesus.
Hosea's words 'not my people' and 'my people' foretell the calling of the Gentiles.
Joel 2:28-32 was fulfilled at Pentecost.
Jesus is the Passover lamb whose death takes away sin.
Isaiah 53:4, 'Himself took our infirmities', was fulfilled in the healings Jesus performed.
Psalm 78:2, 'I will open my mouth in a parable', is a prophecy fulfilled in Jesus's teaching in parables.
Isaiah 6:9-10 foretells that Israel would hear Jesus and not understand.
Isaiah 29:13, 'this people honoureth me with their lips', is a prophecy about those who opposed Jesus.
Zechariah 13:7, 'smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered', foretells the arrest of Jesus and the flight of his disciples.
Psalm 118:26, 'Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD', speaks of Jesus.
Psalm 8:2, 'Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings', was fulfilled when children praised Jesus in the Temple.
Psalm 69:9, 'the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up', foretells Jesus cleansing the Temple.
Daniel's 'abomination of desolation' foretells an event still to come when Jesus spoke.
'They hated me without a cause' in the Psalms is a prophecy of the hatred of Jesus.
Psalms 69:25 and 109:8 foretell the fate of Judas and his replacement.
Psalm 35:11, 'False witnesses did rise up', foretells the false witnesses at the trial of Jesus.
Isaiah 54:13, 'all thy children shall be taught of the LORD', is fulfilled in those who come to Jesus.
Psalm 82:6, 'I have said, Ye are gods', supports Jesus calling himself the Son of God.
Isaiah 53:1, 'Who hath believed our report?', foretells Israel's unbelief in Jesus.
The brass serpent Moses lifted up foreshadows Jesus lifted up on the cross.
Isaiah 53:3 and 49:7 foretell that the Messiah would be despised and rejected by his own people.
Isaiah 53:5, 'he was wounded for our transgressions', foretells Jesus bearing the punishment for sins.
Isaiah 53:7, 'as a lamb to the slaughter', foretells the silence of Jesus before his accusers.
Isaiah 53:8, 'he was cut off out of the land of the living', foretells the death of the Messiah.
Isaiah 53:9, 'with the rich in his death', foretells the burial of Jesus in a rich man's tomb.
Isaiah 53:10 foretells that the Messiah would be an offering for sin and then live again.
Isaiah 53:11, 'shall my righteous servant justify many', teaches justification through the Messiah.
Isaiah 53:12, 'he was numbered with the transgressors', was fulfilled when Jesus was crucified between two thieves.
Isaiah 52:14, 'his visage was so marred', foretells the scourging and disfigurement of Jesus.
Isaiah 50:6, 'I gave my back to the smiters', foretells the scourging and spitting Jesus suffered.
Psalm 22:7-8 foretells the mocking of Jesus on the cross.
Psalm 22:22, 'I will declare thy name unto my brethren', is spoken by Jesus.
Psalm 31:5, 'Into thine hand I commit my spirit', foretells the last words of Jesus.
Amos 8:9, the sun going down at noon, foretells the darkness at the crucifixion.
Isaiah 35:5-6 foretells the healing miracles of Jesus.
Isaiah 11:1-10, the rod out of the stem of Jesse, is fulfilled in Jesus, in whom the Gentiles trust.
Numbers 24:17, 'there shall come a Star out of Jacob', foretells Jesus and the star of Bethlehem.
God's promise to David in 2 Samuel 7:12-16, 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son', is spoken of Jesus.
Isaiah 9:7, the throne of David established for ever, is fulfilled in Jesus.
The promise that all nations would be blessed in Abraham's seed is the gospel preached beforehand.
Psalm 72:10-11 and Isaiah 60:6 foretell the wise men bringing gifts to Jesus.
The name Immanuel, 'God with us', in Isaiah 7:14 shows that the child is God.
Jeremiah 31:22, 'A woman shall compass a man', foretells the virgin birth.
Psalm 2:1-2, the rulers taking counsel against the LORD's anointed, foretells Herod and Pilate against Jesus.
Ezekiel 34:23, the one shepherd, 'my servant David', is Jesus the good shepherd.
The manna in the wilderness foreshadows Jesus, the bread from heaven.
Jacob's ladder foreshadows Jesus, on whom the angels of God ascend and descend.
Isaiah saw the glory of Jesus in his vision of the LORD on the throne.
Isaiah 22:22, the key of the house of David, speaks of Jesus.
The stone cut out without hands in Daniel 2 is the kingdom Jesus founded at his first coming.
Isaiah 25:8 and Hosea 13:14, death swallowed up in victory, are fulfilled in the resurrection through Jesus.
Amos 9:11-12, the tabernacle of David rebuilt, is fulfilled in the Gentiles joining the Church.
Isaiah 49:6 and 42:6, 'a light to the Gentiles', speak of Jesus.
Christ became a curse for us, as it is written, 'he that is hanged is accursed of God'.
'Whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered' in Joel 2:32 means calling on the name of Jesus.
Isaiah 45:23, 'unto me every knee shall bow', is spoken of Jesus.
The stone of stumbling in Isaiah 8:14 and the corner stone in Isaiah 28:16 are Jesus.
Isaiah 59:20-21, 'the Redeemer shall come to Zion', foretells Jesus taking away the sins of Israel.
Isaiah 65:1-2 foretells the Gentiles finding God while Israel refuses.
Deuteronomy 32:21 foretells that God would provoke Israel to jealousy through the Gentile Church.
Isaiah 10:22-23 and 1:9 teach that only a remnant of Israel, those who believe in Jesus, will be saved.
The Scriptures foretold that God would blind Israel so that it would not believe.
Psalm 32:1-2 teaches that God counts a person righteous apart from works.
Psalm 8:4-6, the son of man made a little lower than the angels, speaks of Jesus.
Leviticus 18:5, 'which if a man do, he shall live in them', shows that the Law is not of faith.
Deuteronomy 30:11-14, 'the word is very nigh unto thee', speaks of the word of faith in Christ.
Hagar and Sarah are an allegory of two covenants: Sinai in bondage, and the free children of the promise.
The veil over Moses's face shows that a veil lies on the heart of Israel when the Law is read.
Psalm 19:4, 'their line is gone out through all the earth', shows that Israel has heard the gospel.
Isaiah 52:7, 'How beautiful are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings', speaks of preaching the gospel of Christ.
Isaiah 55:3, 'the sure mercies of David', foretells the resurrection of Jesus.
Psalm 132:11, 'Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne', is God's oath to raise up Christ.
Isaiah 28:11-12, 'with another tongue will he speak to this people', foretells speaking in tongues.
The rock that gave Israel water in the wilderness was Christ.
Psalm 102:25-27, 'of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth', is addressed to the Son.
The Scriptures command all the angels of God to worship the Son.

passages.note: The words quoted in Hebrews are found in the Greek version of this verse.

claims.claim: Isaiah 8:17-18, 'I and the children whom the LORD hath given me', is spoken by Jesus.
Psalm 95:7-11 shows that Joshua did not give Israel rest and that a rest remains, entered through Christ.
The earthly sanctuary and its service were only a shadow of heavenly things.
The sacrifice of Jesus was offered once for all, and no further sacrifice for sin will ever be offered.
The blood of bulls and goats could never take away sins.
Habakkuk 2:3, 'it will surely come', foretells the coming of Jesus: 'he that shall come will come'.
Abraham's offering of Isaac foreshadows God giving his only Son.
The priesthood of Aaron was imperfect and was changed, and with it the Law.
There is one mediator between God and men, and no one comes to the Father except through Jesus.
Abel's offering was accepted because it was a blood sacrifice.
The blood of the covenant at Sinai foreshadows the blood of Jesus, shed for the remission of sins.
The Day of Atonement was fulfilled when Jesus entered the holy place once with his own blood.
Micah 5:2, 'whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting', shows that the Messiah existed from eternity.
Genesis 19:24, 'the LORD rained brimstone from the LORD out of heaven', shows two persons called the LORD.
The three men who appeared to Abraham in Genesis 18 show God appearing in human form, or as three persons.
The Hebrew word for God, Elohim, is plural and so points to more than one person in God.
God says 'us' in Genesis 3:22 and 11:7 and Isaiah 6:8, showing a plurality of persons.
'Holy, holy, holy' in Isaiah 6:3 points to the three persons of the Trinity.
Isaiah 48:16, 'the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me', shows the three persons of the Trinity.
Isaiah 63:9-10, the angel of his presence and his holy Spirit, shows three persons in God.
The Angel of the LORD who speaks as God is Jesus before his birth.
The man who wrestled with Jacob was God in human form.
Zechariah 14:3-4, the LORD's feet standing on the mount of Olives, foretells the return of Jesus.
Zechariah 2:10-11, 'I will dwell in the midst of thee ... the LORD of hosts hath sent me', shows the LORD sent by the LORD.
The fourth man in the furnace, 'like the Son of God', was Jesus.
Wisdom in Proverbs 8:22-31, with God before the creation, is Christ.
The Word by which God created all things is a divine person, who became flesh in Jesus.
Isaiah 44:6, 'the LORD the King of Israel, and his redeemer the LORD of hosts', names two who are the LORD.
Jesus took the divine name of Exodus 3:14 when he said 'Before Abraham was, I am'.
Since God says 'beside me there is no saviour', Jesus the Saviour must be God.
Jesus is to be worshipped and honoured even as the Father is.
Jesus is the only begotten Son of God.
Isaiah 64:6, 'all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags', shows that good deeds are worthless before God.
Jeremiah 17:9, 'The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked', shows that man cannot do good.
Psalm 51:5, 'in sin did my mother conceive me', teaches that everyone is born a sinner.
Genesis 6:5 and 8:21 show that the human heart is wholly evil from birth.
Isaiah 1:18, 'though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow', is fulfilled through the blood of Jesus.
Ezekiel 36:25-27, a new heart and a new spirit, is the new birth that comes through faith in Jesus.
Job 19:25, 'I know that my redeemer liveth', speaks of Jesus.
Hosea 3:4-5 foretells Israel's long years without sacrifice until it turns to Jesus, the son of David.
Hosea 5:15, 'I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence', foretells Jesus's ascension and his return when Israel repents of rejecting him.
Zechariah 6:12-13, the BRANCH who is a priest upon his throne, foretells Jesus as both king and priest.
Zechariah 3:8-9, 'my servant the BRANCH' and iniquity removed in one day, foretells the crucifixion.
The coats of skins God made for Adam and Eve were the first blood sacrifice to cover sin.
Forgiveness of sins comes only through believing in the name of Jesus.
Salvation is by grace through faith, and not by works.
Satan is a rebel angel who fell from heaven, as told in Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28.
The serpent in Eden was Satan.
The dietary laws were abolished: all foods are now clean.
The Sabbath is no longer binding.
Circumcision of the flesh is no longer required; true circumcision is of the heart.
The feasts of Israel were shadows fulfilled in Christ and need no longer be kept.
The kingdom of God was taken from Israel and given to another nation.
The Church is the true Israel, and those who believe in Jesus are the children of Abraham.
The destruction of the Temple and the exile came because Israel rejected Jesus.
God has given a further revelation through his Son that completes the Law and the Prophets.
The miracles of Jesus prove that he is the Messiah and the Son of God.
God's temple is now the body of Christ and his people, not a building in Jerusalem.
